text: The 25.5-hectare tree-cover loss in 2015 was detected by the Hansen Global Forest Change dataset (GFC-2025-v1.13), which tracks stand-replacing tree-cover loss at 30-meter resolution. This event occurred before the 2020 baseline and is classified as historical, meaning it happened outside the claim period (2021–2025). The loss was significant enough to be recorded as an event, unlike smaller patches (under 0.5 ha) that may go undetected due to resolution limits. The JRC 2020 reference map confirms no forest was present in 2020, supporting the historical nature of the loss. The cause isn’t specified, but such losses often result from land-use changes like agriculture, logging, or development.
